route.name: Haifa-Beirut-Tripoli Railway (HBT)
route.description: WWII coastal military line; only Nahariya-Haifa survives
route.notes: Built astonishingly fast (~176 miles completed 20 Dec 1942, ~6 months early); standard gauge throughout.  [route] Coast-hugging alignment south->north: Haifa, Acre, Nahariya, Ras al-Naqoura (the border headland / Rosh HaNikra), Tyre, Sidon, Beirut, Jbeil (Byblos), Chekka, Tripoli. The Haifa-Acre section was dual-gauge (also 1,050 mm).  [connections] Meets the Tripoli-Homs line at Tripoli and, via Haifa/Lydda, the Sinai Military Railway toward Egypt — together these traced the ephemeral WWII standard-gauge corridor from Egypt toward Turkey.  [survival] Only the Nahariya-Haifa section survives and still operates (Israel Railways); the Lebanese coastal section was largely lifted, and the 1948 partition severed the line at Ras al-Naqoura.
route.history: A WWII standard-gauge (1,435 mm) military railway hugging the Mediterranean coast, built Dec 1941-Dec 1942 by the South African Engineering Corps (Haifa-Beirut) and the Australian Railway Construction & Maintenance Group (Beirut-Tripoli), with African Auxiliary Pioneers and up to 8,000 local labourers. The ~176-mile line was completed on 20 December 1942, about six months ahead of schedule; General Alexander drove the final spike at Nahr el-Kelb.
